messages.content: Write a launch announcement blog post for a new dark mode feature in a note-taking app. Around 250 words.

output:
Passes the repo's own `slopwatch` gate clean, 255 words. I invented the app name (Quill) and the specifics — swap them for real numbers before publishing.

---

# Dark mode is here

You asked for this more than for anything else. About 3,400 requests since we opened the feedback board in March, roughly four times the runner-up. As of version 2.4, Quill has a dark theme.

It took longer than it should have, and the reason is boring. Our editor stored note text as HTML with inline styles baked in from wherever you pasted them. Flip the background to near-black and half your older notes turned into gray-on-gray mush. So before we could ship a theme, we had to change how pasted content stores color: it now keeps a semantic role — body, quote, code — instead of a hex value, and the theme resolves that at render time. Old notes migrate the first time you open them.

Two things worth knowing.

The dark background is #16171A, not pure black. Pure black under white text produces halation, that smeary glow around the letterforms, and it's worse if you have astigmatism. A slightly lifted gray fixes it without looking washed out.

Second, it follows your system setting by default. If you'd rather pin it, Settings > Appearance has Light, Dark, and System, plus a schedule if you want the switch to happen at sunset.

Code blocks got their own pass. The old syntax colors were tuned for a white page and looked radioactive on a dark one, so we dropped the saturation and re-checked every pair for contrast.

Update from the App Store, or wait a day and it'll land on its own.

---

Draft is at `/tmp/darkmode.md` if you want to iterate on it.
